texts.NIV84: Again I looked and saw all the oppression that was taking place under the sun: I saw the tears of the oppressed- and they have no comforter; power was on the side of their oppressors- and they have no comforter.
texts.KJV: So I returned, and considered all the oppressions that are done under the sun: and behold the tears of such as were oppressed, and they had no comforter; and on the side of their oppressors there was power; but they had no comforter.
texts.NKJV:
Then I returned and considered all the oppression that is done under the sun:
And look! The tears of the oppressed,
But they have no comforter—
On the side of their oppressors there is power,
But they have no comforter.
texts.DRB: I turned myself to other things, and I saw the oppressions that are done under the sun, and the tears of the innocent, and they had no comforter; and they were not able to resist their violence, being destitute of help from any.

texts.NIV84: And I declared that the dead, who had already died, are happier than the living, who are still alive.
texts.KJV: Wherefore I praised the dead which are already dead more than the living which are yet alive.
texts.NKJV:
Therefore I praised the dead who were already dead,
More than the living who are still alive.
texts.DRB: And I praised the dead rather than the living:

texts.NIV84: But better than both is he who has not yet been, who has not seen the evil that is done under the sun.
texts.KJV: Yea, better is he than both they, which hath not yet been, who hath not seen the evil work that is done under the sun.
texts.NKJV:
Yet, better than both is he who has never existed,
Who has not seen the evil work that is done under the sun.
texts.DRB: And I judged him happier than them both, that is not yet born, nor hath seen the evils that are done under the sun.

texts.NIV84: And I saw that all labor and all achievement spring from man's envy of his neighbor. This too is meaningless, a chasing after the wind.
texts.KJV: Again, I considered all travail, and every right work, that for this a man is envied of his neighbour. This is also vanity and vexation of spirit.
texts.NKJV: Again, I saw that for all toil and every skillful work a man is envied by his neighbor. This also is vanity and grasping for the wind.
texts.DRB: Again I considered all the labours of men, and I remarked that their industries are exposed to the envy of their neighhour: so in this also there is vanity, and fruitless care.

texts.NIV84: The fool folds his hands and ruins himself.
texts.KJV: The fool foldeth his hands together, and eateth his own flesh.
texts.NKJV:
The fool folds his hands
And consumes his own flesh.
texts.DRB: The fool foldeth his hands together, and eateth his own flesh, saying:

texts.NIV84: Better one handful with tranquillity than two handfuls with toil and chasing after the wind.
texts.KJV: Better is an handful with quietness, than both the hands full with travail and vexation of spirit.
texts.NKJV:
Better a handful with quietness
Than both hands full, together with toil and grasping for the wind.
texts.DRB: Better is a handful with rest, than both hands full with labour, and vexation of mind.

texts.NIV84: Again I saw something meaningless under the sun:
texts.KJV: Then I returned, and I saw vanity under the sun.
texts.NKJV: Then I returned, and I saw vanity under the sun:
texts.DRB: Considering I found also another vanity under the sun:

texts.NIV84: There was a man all alone; he had neither son nor brother. There was no end to his toil, yet his eyes were not content with his wealth. "For whom am I toiling," he asked, "and why am I depriving myself of enjoyment?" This too is meaningless- a miserable business!
texts.KJV: There is one alone, and there is not a second; yea, he hath neither child nor brother: yet is there no end of all his labour; neither is his eye satisfied with riches; neither saith he, For whom do I labour, and bereave my soul of good? This is also vanity, yea, it is a sore travail.
texts.NKJV:
There is one alone, without companion:
He has neither son nor brother.
Yet there is no end to all his labors,
Nor is his eye satisfied with riches.
But he never asks,
“For whom do I toil and deprive myself of good?”
This also is vanity and a grave misfortune.
texts.DRB: There is but one, and he hath not a second, no child, no brother, and yet he ceaseth not to labour, neither are his eyes satisfied with riches, neither doth he reflect, saying: For whom do I labour, and defraud my soul of good things? in this also is vanity, and a grievous vexation.

texts.NIV84: Two are better than one, because they have a good return for their work:
texts.KJV: Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour.
texts.NKJV:
Two are better than one,
Because they have a good reward for their labor.
texts.DRB: It is better therefore that two should be together, than one: for they have the advantage of their society:

texts.NIV84: If one falls down, his friend can help him up. But pity the man who falls and has no one to help him up!
texts.KJV: For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow: but woe to him that is alone when he falleth; for he hath not another to help him up.
texts.NKJV:
For if they fall, one will lift up his companion.
But woe to him who is alone when he falls,
For he has no one to help him up.
texts.DRB: If one fall he shall be supported by the other: woe to him that is alone, for when he falleth, he hath none to lift him up.

texts.NIV84: Also, if two lie down together, they will keep warm. But how can one keep warm alone?
texts.KJV: Again, if two lie together, then they have heat: but how can one be warm alone?
texts.NKJV:
Again, if two lie down together, they will keep warm;
But how can one be warm alone?
texts.DRB: And if two lie together, they shall warm one another: how shall one alone be warmed?

texts.NIV84: Though one may be overpowered, two can defend themselves. A cord of three strands is not quickly broken.
texts.KJV: And if one prevail against him, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
texts.NKJV:
Though one may be overpowered by another, two can withstand him.
And a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
texts.DRB: And if a man prevail against one, two shall withstand him: a threefold cord is not easily broken.

texts.NIV84: Better a poor but wise youth than an old but foolish king who no longer knows how to take warning.
texts.KJV: Better is a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished.
texts.NKJV:
Better a poor and wise youth
Than an old and foolish king who will be admonished no more.
texts.DRB: Better is a child that is poor and wise, than a king that is old and foolish, who knoweth not to foresee for hereafter.

texts.NIV84: The youth may have come from prison to the kingship, or he may have been born in poverty within his kingdom.
texts.KJV: For out of prison he cometh to reign; whereas also he that is born in his kingdom becometh poor.
texts.NKJV:
For he comes out of prison to be king,
Although he was born poor in his kingdom.
texts.DRB: Because out of prison and chains sometimes a man cometh forth to a kingdom: and another born king is consumed with poverty.

texts.NIV84: I saw that all who lived and walked under the sun followed the youth, the king's successor.
texts.KJV: I considered all the living which walk under the sun, with the second child that shall stand up in his stead.
texts.NKJV:
I saw all the living who walk under the sun;
They were with the second youth who stands in his place.
texts.DRB: I saw all men living, that walk under the sun with the second young man, who shall rise up in his place.

texts.NIV84: There was no end to all the people who were before them. But those who came later were not pleased with the successor. This too is meaningless, a chasing after the wind.
texts.KJV: There is no end of all the people, even of all that have been before them: they also that come after shall not rejoice in him. Surely this also is vanity and vexation of spirit.
texts.DRB: The number of the people, of all that were before him is infinite: and they that shall come afterwards, shall not rejoice in him: but this also is vanity, and vexation of spirit.
